statement: Throughout this statement, an integer i is an a-match if 0 <= i, i + la <= n, and s[i..i+la-1] = a (i.e., s[i+t] = a[t] for every t with 0 <= t < la); an integer j is a b-match if 0 <= j, j + lb <= n, and s[j..j+lb-1] = b (i.e., s[j+t] = b[t] for every t with 0 <= t < lb); and i is beautiful if i is an a-match and there exists a b-match j with |j - i| <= k. The function returns a result r (a Vec of i64) such that: (a) for every integer i, i occurs in r (i.e., there is t with 0 <= t < len(r) and r[t] = i) iff i is beautiful; and (b) for every t with 0 <= t and t+1 < len(r), r[t] < r[t+1]. Equivalently, r is exactly the strictly increasing list of all beautiful indices.
